office_does: State Representatives write and vote on state laws and the state budgets; this seat is one of two House seats for District 28 in Pierce County.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Dan Bronoske, a fire captain in the House since 2021, faces Kerry Hills, a probation officer who prefers the Nonpartisan Party. Hills was not on the primary ballot; filing dates and the 9.3 percent write-in share suggest a write-in qualification, but no by-name tally was found.

candidates.summary: West Pierce Fire & Rescue captain and chair of the House Health Care & Wellness Committee, in the House since 2021, running on lower costs, health care and public safety.
highlights: One of eight House Democrats to vote against ESSB 6346; voted for the 2025 capital gains, B&O and gas tax bills [S5][S11][S13][S19][S25]
Voted against the final 2025 rent-increase limit and favors permit streamlining and more housing types [S2][S17]
Cites capping a 30-day insulin supply at $35 [S2]

taxes.basis: Split record: no on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5814; yes on ESSB 5813, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5801.

spending.basis: Cites investments in teachers, mental health, school nutrition, public transit and Medicaid reimbursement.

housing.basis: Favors more supply through permit streamlining and more housing types; voted against the House and final versions of the 2025 rent-increase limit, though for concurring in the looser Senate version.

safety.basis: Pairs law enforcement training investment with accountability and behavioral health resources.

healthcare.basis: Works on cost caps such as $35 insulin and lower drug prices within the existing system; no single-payer position.

experience.basis: In the House since 2021 and chair of the Health Care & Wellness Committee.

social.basis: Voted for ESSB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care; no statements found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list and for ESSB 5599; no statements on the topic.

candidates.summary: Lakewood probation officer and former clinical case manager who prefers the Nonpartisan Party, running on concern over tax increases and state spending.
highlights: Has "great concern about the increased taxes enacted" [S1]
Says "Olympia has a spending problem" and lacks fiscal responsibility [S1]
Was not on the primary ballot; filing dates and write-in totals suggest a write-in qualification, though no by-name tally was found [S2][S3][S4]

taxes.basis: Expresses 'great concern about the increased taxes enacted' without naming a tax or pledge.

spending.basis: Says Olympia 'has a spending problem' and lacks fiscal responsibility.

experience.basis: No public office; elected experience is a school parent board and an HOA presidency.
